pharmacology.text: Fluparoxan is a very selective α2-adrenergic blocker, that readily crosses the blood–brain barrier. Blockade of α2-adrenoreceptors, particularly presynaptic autoreceptors in noradrenergic neurons, by fluparoxan produces an increase in the synaptic concentrations of noradrenaline by blocking the autoinhibitory feedback mechanism.

body.says: Greater than 90% excreted as (sulphamic acid and carbamoyI glucuronide conjugates)

uses.text: Fluparoxan (developmental code name GR50360A) is a potent α2-adrenergic receptor antagonist (pKB = 7.9) with excellent selectivity for this receptor over the α1-adrenergic receptor (2,630-fold), and is the only well-studied α2-adrenergic receptor antagonist in its structural family which does not antagonize any variant of the imidazoline receptor.
